note: What the website shows for each game's mod: its version and what changed. A game's optional "settings" (launcher checkboxes or dropdowns, format in the launcher's CONFIG.md, "Game settings") are copied into catalog.json by tools/update-catalog.ps1. Edit this by hand when a game file changes; the file dates, sizes and checksums come from catalog.json. Bump the version whenever the online file is replaced.

changes: The online panel opens on ONLINE (room codes) by default.
Every player has their own camera (Ruffle Together 1.0.3.7 or newer): each PC follows its own player, the HUD stays on screen.
Co-op for 2 to 4 players: local co-op added to the game, every PC plays with its normal keys; players 2 to 4 are tinted red, green and blue.
Lock-picks and doors work for every player.
Lobby mode: the launcher's lobby runs the room.
Fixes the levels that would not start outside the web page.

Turns setting for the launcher (--coop-option turns=stick): turn rotation, the default, passes each team's turns round all its players, so a fourth player plays even when the team has three sticks; by stick gives each player their own sticks.
Each player plays only their own sticks on their own turns: nobody else's keys or clicks move them, the host's included (Ruffle Together 1.0.3.7+).
Ruffle Together: plays the game's own Player 1 vs Player 2 hot-seat online with 2-4 players, no netcode in the game (launcher, --coop-keys territory-war).
Network version tw-2: everyone in a room needs this build (older builds are refused with a clear message).
Direct IP mode next to room codes (MODE button; room codes stay the default).
A second match in the same room works: the friends' sticks no longer go to the host.
The turn menu is dimmed while someone else has the turn.
Ruffle Together: VS Human online for 2 PCs, no netcode in the game (launcher, --coop-keys bow-man, Ruffle Together 1.0.3.6+).
Keys: player 1 W/S to aim and Space to draw and shoot, player 2 I/K and Enter (on your own PC: W/S or the arrows, Space/Enter/F).
Each player can also aim their own archer with their own mouse.
Replaces the room-code/Direct IP online mod (VS Online menu).
Every player in the Ruffle Together session gets a ship (2 to 4), with no join step.
Everyone plays with the game's own keys on their own PC: arrows, A to fire, Ctrl, 1-3, Y/N.
A friend who leaves loses their ship and the others play on.
Needs Ruffle Together 1.0.3.8 or later.
Local co-op for one to four players, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.3.4 (--coop-keys air-battle).
PLAYERS 1-4 on the main menu; every boat has its own keys and balloon colour.
Extra boats wait at the start until their player presses a key; the level fails only when every boat is down.
Replaces the relay mod (room codes); one player is the original game.
A friend who leaves no longer stalls the game: their turns are skipped, and a turn they were aiming goes to the next player.
The player count follows the room: PLAYERS starts at the number of people in it and can't go above it.
The turn banner shows the player's name.
Tested on Ruffle Together 1.0.4.
Every player can buy rockets, grenades and the raft upgrade in the shop with their own mouse, and press DONE.
Tested on Ruffle Together 1.0.3.6.
Every player aims and fires with their own mouse on their turn (Ruffle Together 1.0.3.4+); keys still work.
Online co-op for two to four players, taking turns.
Online co-op for up to four players through the campaign, room codes or Direct IP.
The game's own 2-player co-op online through Ruffle Together 1.0.3.6 (--coop-keys fireboy-watergirl): the host is Fireboy, the friend is Watergirl.
No ad, online hiscore board or sponsor links (there is no network inside a session).
Back to one shared screen for everyone; the per-player camera setting is gone.
The game's own keys for everyone: arrows, A to punch, S for the second punch, each on their own PC.
Each player's name under their HUD.
Friendly fire, off unless the host turns it on (--coop-option friendlyfire=1).
A friend who leaves is removed from the game.
Every player has their own HUD at the top left like player 1's (portrait, rage, health), tinted like their character.
Ruffle Together 1.0.3.7: a friend who leaves is taken out of the game and the others play on.
Players 2-4 added to the single-player game, online through Ruffle Together (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4): each on their own keys; the host clicks the menus.
Enemies and bosses go for the nearest player; one shared screen follows the group; a knocked-out player gets up after 6 seconds while anyone is still standing.
With 1 player it is the original game.

1.2: the campaign with friends: every player in the session gets their own fighter on player 1's side in all 15 levels and the ending, with their own card's look, keys and a name tag; a level is lost only when every player is out of lives, and level 4's score is the team's. Survival stays single-player.

1.1: 2 to 6 players through Ruffle Together 1.0.5: players 3-6 take the game's other four fighters (CPUs in the original), each on their own PC's keys, with a name tag over it; each friend clicks only their own card on the players page.
The game's own 2-player Deathmatch online through Ruffle Together 1.0.3.8 (--coop-keys chaos-faction-2): Keyboard 1 and Keyboard 2 on two PCs, plus the CPU fighters.
Both players use the game's own keys on their own PC (arrows, Z, X, D, Shift, T); the host's Space pauses and the host's mouse runs the menus.
Player 2 starts as Keyboard 2 in a session.
With 1 player it is the original game.

Players 2-4 added to the single-player brawler, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.3.9+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4; the game sets its own keys): arrows, A to punch, S to kick, each on their own PC; the host clicks the menus.
Each player tinted, with their own health portrait at the top left and their name over their head.
One shared screen: walking scrolls the street for everyone and never pushes a friend off the screen.
Enemies go for the nearest player who is up; a player out of health gets up 8 seconds later with half health while anyone is standing; everyone down is the game's own game over.
A friend who leaves is removed and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.
1.1: a teammate who is off your screen gets an arrow at the edge in their colour, with their name and distance, so nobody seems to vanish when one player runs ahead.
Players 2-4 added to the single-player shooter, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.3.8 (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4; the game sets its own keys).
Every player walks, jumps, uses and reloads on their own keys and aims and shoots with their own mouse.
A camera per player: each PC follows its own hero (or one shared team camera, a host setting), with a zoom setting.
A panel per player (health, armor, weapon, ammo, coins, aidkits), names over the heroes, players 2-4 tinted.
Enemies go for any hero; everyone picks up coins, items and weapons for themselves; missions count for the team; whoever reaches the exit takes the team on.
A downed player gets up next to a friend with jump; everyone down: the checkpoint or a restart, as in the original.
Shops use the coins and the mouse of the player who opened them.
Friendly fire and players bumping into each other are off unless the host turns them on.
A friend who leaves is removed and the rest play on. With 1 player it is the original game.
1.1: deaths are shown per player in the top bar, set out by the player count, and on the finish screen; the footer only shows who has reached the goal.

Players 2-4 added to the single-player game, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.6+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4): arrows or WASD, each on their own PC; the host clicks the menus and the continue screens.
Each player is a square of their own colour with their name above it; each player's deaths are in the top bar in their colour, in place of the team total.
Every player has their own checkpoint. Coins are shared, and the coins you took go back when you die.
A level ends when all coins are taken and everyone stands in the goal together.
A friend who leaves is removed, the coins they took stay taken, and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.

Players 2-4 added to the single-player game, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4): arrows or WASD, each on their own PC; the host clicks the menus and the CONTINUE screens.
Each player is a square in one of the game's colours with their name above it, and their deaths in the top bar.
Every player has their own checkpoint and dies on their own. Coins are shared, and a coin goes back when the player who took it dies.
Any player can take a key; its door stays open for the level.
A level ends when all coins are taken and everyone stands in the goal together.
A friend who leaves is removed, the coins they took stay taken, and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.
1.1: the game no longer goes dead when you leave the training or at the end of a fight. Needs Ruffle Together 1.0.7, where your keyboard follows the game's own keys.

Players 2-4 added to the single-player fighter, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.7+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4): arrows, A, S, D, W, Q, E, each on their own PC; the host clicks the menus.
A team fights the whole tournament in one arena, each player in their own colour with their own health, battery and name.
Enemies go for their nearest player who is up, with one extra enemy per extra player.
A player out of health stays down until the match ends; the match is lost only when everyone is down.
A friend who leaves is removed and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.

Players 2-4 added to the single-player game, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4): arrows or WASD to move and Space or Z to jump, each on their own PC; the host clicks the menus.
Player 1 plays the character picked in the menu; players 2-4 get Sonic, Tails or Knuckles, each with a name tag.
One shared screen follows the team; nobody leaves it, and a player held back for 3 seconds jumps to the one in front.
Rings and lives are the team's. A player who dies comes back next to a friend after 3 seconds; the act restarts only when nobody is left. Passing the finish sign takes the whole team out.
A friend who leaves is removed and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.

2 to 4 players online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4): every player runs their own copy of the game in the same session, with their own Runner or Skater, level and camera, on the game's own keys on their own PC (arrows or A/D, Space/Up/W to jump, R to restart).
Friends pick Runner with Left and Skater with Right, and start from the host's unlocked levels.
Only the host's game plays music; only the host can pause and use the mouse (editor, options).
A friend who leaves is removed and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.

2 to 4 players online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4): every player runs their own copy of the game in the same session, with their own runner, level and camera, on their own PC's keys (arrows or A/D, Space/Up/W to jump).
Everyone starts the mode and level the host picks with the mouse, then plays at their own pace; when the host starts another game, everyone switches to it.
Each player takes a new costume with their own jump key; only the host's game plays music; only the host can pause and use the mouse.
A friend who leaves is removed and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.

A second player added to the single-player game, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2): each player has their own kid and uses arrows and Space on their own PC; the host clicks the menus.
Chainsaw floor: each kid walks and saws on their own; whoever reaches the edge scrolls the screen and the other is dragged along.
Shootout and boss floors: the kids walk as a team, and each ducks, shoots or saws on their own; one shared health bar, and a shot hurts every kid standing.
In co-op the boss always dies when sawn (the original can get stuck there when Space is held with no key repeat).
A friend who leaves is removed and the other plays on.
With 1 player it is the original game.
1.4: a friend's thrown hook comes back. Before, it never did, and that friend couldn't use doors, swap or pick up for the rest of the stage.
1.3: a body that slid down stairs into a box no longer keeps a room locked for good.
1.2: stage 1-H can be finished with friends: player 2's aim no longer removes the point the Mag boss retreats to.

1.1: the game's own keys now work for every player: Q swap, Space dodge and use, R reload, E pick up, Shift bullet time, WASD or arrows. Before, Space was on X and Q on Z, and R, E and Shift did nothing. Needs the launcher's new start map, stealth-hunter-2.

Players 2-4 added to the single-player game in Story and Arena, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.6+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4; the game sets its own keys): each player on the game's own keys and own mouse, on their own PC.
A camera, HUD and aim per player, and each player's name over their character. Friends play a character of their own with the leader's stats and gear, and can click the menus.
Any player can use doors and panels; a door takes the team along. Enemies target every player; bullet time from anyone slows the world.
A player who dies gets up after 8 seconds while anyone else is up; everyone down is the game's own rule (a life, or mission failed).
A friend who leaves becomes an AI teammate and the rest play on.
With 1 player it is the original game.
Two players on two PCs through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys bow-man, --coop-players 2): the host plays blue, the friend plays red in place of the computer.
Each player moves only their own pieces, on their own turn, with their own mouse, as in the original.
Castling, promotion, check, checkmate and stalemate for both sides, as the game has them for the player.
"YOU MOVE" and the win message show on the screen they belong to; the move list's first line says whose move it is.
If the friend leaves, the computer plays red again and the host plays on.
With 1 player it is the original game.
Players 2-4 added to the single-player shooter, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4; the game sets its own keys).
Every player has their own soldier on the game's own keys and their own mouse to aim and shoot.
A camera per player that looks ahead toward their aim, and each friend's own health, shield and gun in the top bar.
Quick Match and both campaigns: friends on the host's team in the campaign and team modes, everyone against everyone in Deathmatch and Juggernaut; a match is won when any player reaches the score.
Friends respawn by themselves; a friend who leaves takes their soldier with them and the rest play on. With 1 player it is the original game.

1.1: every player has their own portal pair in their own colours (purple/red, green/lime, pink/white for players 2-4); anyone travels through anyone's portals, and a portal can't land on another portal. Each player's arm and gun now point at their own mouse.
Players 2-4 added to the single-player puzzle game, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4; the game sets its own keys).
Every player has their own test subject on the game's own keys and their own mouse to aim the portal gun, with their own crosshair and name.
Buttons, boxes, turrets and every hazard work for every player; each player carries their own box.
One death restarts the chamber for everyone; the next chamber starts when everyone is through the exit. A friend who leaves is removed and the rest play on. With 1 player it is the original game.
Players 2-4 added to the single-player shooter, online through Ruffle Together 1.0.8+ (--coop-keys gun-mayhem-2, --coop-players 2-4; the game sets its own keys).
Every friend gets their own soldier next to the bots, on the game's own keys and their own mouse to aim and fire.
A camera and crosshair per player, and on a friend's PC their own health, ammo and killstreak panel.
Quick Match in every mode (friends on the host's team in team modes), the campaign and the challenges; a friend's soldier is the host's saved class one to three places after the host's.
A friend who leaves stays down and the rest play on. With one player it is the original game.
